newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves new West Bank settlement housing.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves new West Bank settlement housing.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai has approved a plan to build 1,800 more homes in a Jewish settlement in the West Bank, drawing fire on Wednesday from Palestinians and Israeli peace activists.

"This is not just a violation of signed accords but time bombs and mines planted in the path of anyone who dares to pursue the peace process," chief Palestinian peace negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters.

News of Mordechai's decision, described by his office as approval of plans ratified and then frozen by the previous Labour-led government, broke hours before he was due to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for the first time, in Gaza.

Pinhas Wallerstein, head of the Council of Jewish Settlers, said the 1,800 housing units would be built in Matityahu, a settlement for ultra-orthodox Jews near the pre-1967 Middle East war border between Israel and the West Bank.

"This is the largest approval to build since the government was formed and overturned the freeze on settlement building," Peace Now spokesman Alon Arnon told Reuters, estimating the current population of Matityahu at 2,400.

"This is surprising and worrying that before the Mordechai-Arafat meeting permission is given for such a large expansion of settlements...and raises questions as to the government's intentions," he said.
Mordechai's moves were in line with the decision by the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to nullify the previous administration's building freeze in the West Bank.

"It received all the permits from the previous government and I am glad the defence minister finally approved it," Wallerstein told Army Radio. "I understand that once all the planning stages are completed, the investor can start building."

A Defence Ministry spokeswoman declined to confirm the 1,800 unit figure but said: "we are speaking of plans which were approved in the past by the previous government and frozen and now they have been reapproved."
Palestinian Minister of Supplies Abdel-Aziz Shaheen railed against Mordechai's decision.

"We should have stronger mass confrontation. The Palestinian people should go out to continue their struggle against the Zionist project which is to settle everywhere in Gaza and the West Bank...even if it leads to violence," he told Reuters.

Palestinians want to establish an independent state in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. Some 130,000 Jews have settled amidst the nearly two million Palestinians in the territories since Israel captured them in the 1967 Middle East war.

In a related matter, the Israeli human rights group B'Tselem demanded Mordechai rescind a ban prohibiting Palestinians from travelling on a new bypass road in the West Bank that links Jewish settlements with Jerusalem.
"We view with grave concern the discriminatory restriction imposed on Palestinians with permits to enter Israel," B'Tselem said in a letter to the defence minister.
"Permitting only Jews to use the road contravenes principles of international law, justice and morality," the group said.
